text: dsh-nu 为 DeepSeek Harness 的 TUI 和 Web 配置提供 Nushell 执行环境。它替换平台 shell executor，保留 DSH 的 bash/pwsh 工具入口，并将命令交给 nu 执行。调用前会检查 Nushell 语法和外部 shell handoff，还可向系统提示加入规则、语法指南与提示信息，并改写 shell 工具说明。适合希望在 DSH 中统一使用 Nushell 的开发者；需要兼容版本的 DSH、Node.js 和 Nushell，可用 DSH_NU_PATH 指定 nu。

dsh-nu runs DeepSeek Harness shell calls through Nushell in TUI and Web profiles. It replaces the platform executor, checks syntax and shell handoffs before commands run, and adds Nushell guidance to the system prompt. It requires compatible DSH, Node.js, and Nushell; DSH_NU_PATH selects nu.

dsh-nu 的功能「executor」：让 DSH shell 调用通过 Nushell 执行。由 DSH bundle 挂载后在 shell 调用或提示组装时自动生效。
dsh-nu 的功能「preflight」：执行命令前检查 Nushell 语法及外部 shell handoff。由 DSH bundle 挂载后在 shell 调用或提示组装时自动生效。
dsh-nu 的功能「guide」：向系统提示添加 Nushell 规则和语法指南。由 DSH bundle 挂载后在 shell 调用或提示组装时自动生效。
dsh-nu 的功能「descriptions」：改写 bash/pwsh 工具描述中的 shell 说明为 Nushell。由 DSH bundle 挂载后在 shell 调用或提示组装时自动生效。
dsh-nu 需要兼容版本的 Nushell；默认启动时会探测版本并验证 AST 预检能力，检查不可用时按配置拒绝命令。

dsh-nu README · dsh-nu：[](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-nu)

English | [中文](docs/zh/README.md)

dsh-nu forces DeepSeek Harness to run every shell command in Nushell, with the `bash` / `pwsh` executors disabled. It does three things:

dsh-nu README · dsh-nu：- **Swap the executor**: Through the low-level extension point DeepSeek Harness exposes, it replaces the `bash` / `pwsh` executor with a Nushell executor at runtime (commands run as `nu --no-config-file -c "<command>"`). dsh still sees the same `bash` / `pwsh` tool with the same calling convention, so the Nushell executor plugs into dsh and stays compatible with every other plugin and feature. The oddity is cosmetic: the model calls a tool named `bash` / `pwsh` and passes it Nushell script.
- **Teach the model**: It adds a short Nushell rules section and syntax guide to the system prompt. That teaching text costs some context but matters: with it turned off, the model hits frequent errors when calling the shell tool.
- **Refuse handoffs**: When a Nushell command hands work to another shell, the guard refuses it before a process starts. Bash and PowerShell syntax that Nushell rejects or silently misreads is refused by the syntax rules, with the Nushell spelling in the error.
dsh-nu README · Status：0.7.0 is published on npm. dsh `0.2.2-alpha.2` and Nushell `0.116.1` are the tested pair, recorded in `package.json` under `testedWith`.

dsh-nu README · Compatibility：dsh-nu supports only that pair. The peer ranges cover the dsh family, and boot logs a warning if the installed dsh or Nushell differs. Other versions have not been tested.

dsh-nu README · Install：Requires Node 24.9+, `pnpm` on `PATH` (the `dsh plugin` installer runs it), dsh `0.2.2-alpha.2`, and Nushell `0.116.1` on `PATH`.

Add the bundle to a dsh profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile tui add dsh-nu@0.7.0
```

dsh-nu README · Install：Use `--profile web` for the browser app. The first `dsh plugin` call creates the profile; the bundle's patch disables the platform shell executors, mounts the Nushell executor and teaching layer, and re-mounts the shell tool with a Nushell description. Start the profile with `dsh tui` (or `dsh web`).

If pnpm reports `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION` for a fresh release, it is applying `minimumReleaseAge`. Wait for the cutoff, or add `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0` to the same command.

dsh-nu README · Development：The repository ships a flake with the tested Node and Nushell versions:

```sh
nix develop
```

Inside the shell, or with your own Node 24 and Nushell 0.116.1:

```sh
npm install
node dev/link-peers.mjs --root <dsh-install-root>
npm run typecheck
npm test

`dev/link-peers.mjs` links the dsh peer packages into `node_modules`, so the tests can drive the real seams without publishing.

The suite runs on Node 24. The package requires Node 24.9 and newer.
dsh-nu README · Development：Real-model teaching evals are separate from `npm test`; see [`eval/README.md`](./eval/README.md) for the three-arm harness, cross-model judging, and the dated results.

dsh-nu README · Nix：`nix build` produces that `dsh` binary. `mkDshNuPackage` needs only the dsh installation's `@deepseek-ai` peer packages, so `llm-agents.nix`'s dsh works there too; applying the bundle still needs a wrapper that adds `--patch`, which `nur-ryan4yin`'s `withPlugins` provides. Bump the bundle with `nix flake update dsh-nu`.

dsh-nu README · Configuration：The bundle's patch mounts the shell executor, the shell tool row (`nu-tool-bash` on POSIX, `nu-tool-pwsh` on Windows), and the teaching layer. A profile patch overrides any of them by id. This profile patch spells out every field and its default:

```yaml
- id: nu-executor
  name: dsh-nu/executor
  config:
    nuPath: ""

dsh-nu README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `nuPath` | `$DSH_NU_PATH`, then `nu` | Nushell executable: field, then environment, then PATH |
| `nuArgs` | `["--no-config-file","-c"]` | Argv prefix; the command is appended last, so it must end with `-c` or `--commands` |
| `enforceNushellOnly` | `true` | Refuse handing the command to another shell |
| `foreignShellAllowlist` | `[]` | Regexes exempt from both preflight checks; each must match the whole command |
| `syntaxLint` | `true` | Refuse bash/PowerShell syntax before spawning |
| `syntaxHints` | `true` | Append one `Nushell hint (…)` for a recognized failure or deprecation warning, including exit 0 |
| `guide` | `full` | Prompt guide: `full`, `compact`, or `off` |
| `rules` | `true` | Prepend the shell-rules section |
| `rewriteToolDescriptions` (shell tool) | `true` | Replace the shell claims in the `bash` / `pwsh` tool description, keeping the host's own contract text |
| `enableRunInBackground` / `promoteOnTimeout` (shell tool) | `true` / `true` | dsh's own `tool-bash` / `tool-pwsh` settings, passed through unchanged |
| `rewriteToolDescriptions` (teaching) | `true` | Replace the same shell cla

dsh-nu README · Configuration：Both checks read Nushell's parser through two read-only probes on a private temporary script. Boot runs a token and diagnostic canary once when `verifyNu` is on and either check is enabled: with `requireNu` (the default) a failure fails boot, and with `requireNu: false` each call is refused instead of running without the check (fail closed). The error names `enforceNushellOnly: false` and `syntaxLint: false` as the escape hatches and points at the tested Nushell version.

dsh-nu README · Configuration：Choose the guide by goal:

- `off` disables the guide only; the rules stay on unless `rules: false`. It is a diagnostic baseline: the eval recorded many preflight refusals and extra retries, so do not use it in normal sessions.
- `compact` covers the common idioms and uses fewer prompt tokens. It handled most eval samples without a refusal.
- `full` keeps the detailed syntax reference for uncommon syntax and edge cases.

dsh-nu README · Configuration：Sandbox budgets (`cwd`, `timeoutMs`, …) stay on the `nu-executor` row, not in dsh's shared `shell` settings namespace. Override any row by id in the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`. `examples/preset-nu-shell.md` lists the preset-level shell bypasses to disable.

dsh-nu README · Configuration：The shell tool rows run dsh's own `bash` / `pwsh` tool and change only the description it registers, so the tool name, arguments, and results are dsh's. dsh's settings for its `tool-bash` / `tool-pwsh` rows go on `nu-tool-bash` / `nu-tool-pwsh`. Native function calls and dsh's PTC executor read the same registered description, so switching a profile to PTC needs no dsh-nu setting.
dsh-nu README · What "only Nushell" does not cover：The guard is not a sandbox: it checks command positions it can read, and everything else is out of reach.

dsh-nu README · What "only Nushell" does not cover：- A shell name inside a plain quoted string is data, not a command position: `'bash -c "echo hi"'` evaluates to a string, it does not run bash. `$"…"` and `$'…'` interpolate, so each parenthesized expression inside one is inspected as code; quoted text inside it stays data.
- A literal `nu -c '<script>'` or `nu -e '<script>'` is inspected recursively, up to four levels. A script value built at run time is not inspected.
- A Nushell script file is not read: `nu script.nu`, `source`, and `use` load code the guard never sees, so a handoff written into a file and run that way is out of reach.
- A shell name computed at run time, or a program that starts a shell itself (a language runtime, an editor), is out of reach. The guard follows literal shell names, a fixed launcher table (including `nix shell` / `nix develop --command` and `nix run`), `run-external`, and literal `nu -c` scripts.
- A tool that runs its own argument text is out of scope on purpose: `hyperfine`, `watch`, `make`, `npm run`, and `git` hooks are not shell handoffs, so the guard allows them even though they may start `sh` internally. Refusing them would break the tools
